To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we found that patients with GLUT1DS showed increased neuronal activity in specific cortical areas and the putamen, and that this activity was related to GSWDs and to the level of glycorrhacia at diagnosis.

the BOLD dynamics related with GSWD in patients with GLUTDS are substantially different than typical GGE, showing an increased activity in premotor-striata networks and decreased activity in the thalamo-cortical network, which may represent imaging biomarkers that can help in a precocious diagnosis.

we investigated the brain correlates of GSWD in patients with GLUT 1 deficiency syndrome (a rare disease) and we found that the BOLD dynamics related GSWD in this genetic disorder is substantially different from the typical genetic generalized epilepsy showing the former an increase in the premotor and striatal networks and a decrease in thalamus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying GSWD in patients with GLUT-1 deficiency.
the identification of imaging biomarkers of GSWD in a group of patients affected by GLUT1 deficiency syndrome and compared to a control group of GGE patients.
the development of an imaging biomarker of a rare genetic disorder, which is potentially useful for a precise early diagnosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GLUT1DS and GGE show different BOLD dynamics related with GSWD.
GLUT1DS and GGE have different BOLD dynamics related with GSWD, and that the latter is associated to the level of glycorrhagia.

the present findings support the hypothesis of a different pathophysiology between GGE and GLUT1DS, and that the BOLD signal changes associated with GSWD might provide an imaging biomarker of the GLUT1DS syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel imaging signature for GLUT1 deficiency syndrome, a rare but potentially treatable cause of epilepsy.
we have identified brain regions that are involved in the pathophysiology of GSWD in patients with GLUTDS and GGE.
we found different brain regions involved in the pathogenesis of the GSWD in GGE compared to GLUT1DS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the BOLD dynamics related with GSWD in GLU1DS is substantially different from typical Genetic Generalized Epilesy, and this might represent imaging biomarker of this genetic disorder, being potentially useful in the early diagnosis.
the hemodynamic maps of interictal GWS discharges in GLUT 1 deficiency syndrome (GSWD) are substantially different from the typical GSWD in genetic generalized epilepsy (GGE).
GSWD in GGE and GLUT1DS patients are associated with different BOLD dynamics.
